gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, in named reviewers' own use with the always-on display on, the Amazfit Active Max lasted about 10 days (Basic Tutorials) and the Bip 6 lasted 8 days (Gizbot, Droid.tools). So neither reaches two weeks with the always-on display on, and only the Active Max gets there (about 13–14 days) once it is turned off.
standout_why: I opened The Gadgeteer's under-$200 roundup (rank 10). Every battery figure in it is a maker claim: Bip 6 'up to 14 days', Active 2 '10 days'. Our own page and ChatGPT's answers show only rated figures (25/13 days, 14/6 days) and say 'manufacturer estimates, not guarantees', with no measured day count. I could not read the cited Tom's Guide Bip 6 vs SE 3 piece (the page returned only its title) or the Yahoo Tech roundup (403). Tom's Guide is an 'I tested' article and may hold a Bip 6 battery observation, so the score allows for that. The cited Amazfit Bip 6 product page carries maker claims only.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's and our Active Max pick and turns 'more headroom' into a rule the shopper can act on. With the always-on display on, both watches fall short of 14 days in reviewers' use: Active Max about 10 days, Bip 6 8 days. With it off, the Active Max reaches about 13–14 days (Basic Tutorials: 10 days plus 3–4). The Bip 6 at $79.99 suits shoppers who can charge weekly. Anyone who needs a true two weeks should buy the Active Max and turn off the always-on display.
